decision.observation: 8 mph, gear 1, timer 48:19.703, red X lit. The car is on the gravel's upper edge beside the white paddock fence with cows and red barns above; its nose points up-frame at the fence while the road body runs across to the lower-right of the frame.
decision.hypothesis: The nose is aimed at the fence, not along the road, so a right steer is needed to align with the gravel before the fence is reached; at 8 mph a ~0.9 s W+D beat should be enough to swing it without the stall risk of higher speeds.
decision.memory: The courtyard W+A beat escaped cleanly onto the gravel, confirming short low-speed steer beats work in tight spaces. Nose-vs-road misalignment from an escape is common - fix heading first, then build speed.
